channel.title: EngineerzCorneR — Posts
channel.description: Deep-dive technical write-ups across Electrical, Mechanical, HVAC, Automation, Civil and Solar.

item.title: 4-20mA Current Loops: Why Industry Still Trusts an Analog Signal
item.description: Why 4-20mA beat 0-20mA and voltage signals for instrumentation, what live-zero actually protects against, how to convert a reading back to engineering units.

item.title: Control Valve Components Explained
item.description: What every part of a control valve actually does — body, trim (plug & seat), stem, packing, bonnet, actuator, and positioner — component by component, in the order a signal turns into a throttled flow.

item.title: P&ID (Piping & Instrumentation Diagram) Explained
item.description: How to actually read a P&ID — equipment, piping, valves, instrumentation tags, and signal lines — plus the ISA tag-naming logic and how a P&ID differs from a PFD.

item.title: Cavitation vs. Flashing in Control Valves: What's the Difference?
item.description: Cavitation and flashing both start with the same vapor-pressure event inside a control valve — what happens downstream is what makes one loud and pitted, and the other quiet and eroded.

item.title: Control Valve Cv Sizing: Why Oversizing Is the Most Common Mistake
item.description: Basic incompressible-flow control valve Cv sizing, and why an oversized valve hurts controllability even when it comfortably passes the required flow.

item.title: Erosional vs. Economic Velocity: Which One Actually Sizes Your Pipe?
item.description: Two different velocity limits compete to size a process line — economic velocity minimizes lifecycle cost, the API RP 14E erosional velocity protects the pipe wall. The lower of the two always governs.

item.title: Conventional vs. Balanced Bellows vs. Pilot-Operated PSV: Choosing a Relief Valve Type
item.description: Three ways a pressure relief valve holds its disc shut until set pressure — how back pressure, operating margin, and dirty service tolerance decide between a conventional, balanced bellows, or pilot-operated PSV.

item.title: Pipe Routing Guide: 13 Rules Every Layout Should Follow
item.description: Pipe routing principles, pump suction line routing, equipment clearance, pipe racks, supports, dead legs, expansion loops, hot/cold line routing, utility routing, underground vs above ground, nozzle orientation, flange accessibility, and maintenance clearances.

item.title: Power Transformer, CT & PT: Internal Construction
item.description: The internal construction of a power transformer, a current transformer (CT), and a potential transformer (PT/VT) — parts, typical ratings, accuracy classes, and a side-by-side comparison.

item.title: Battery SoC vs DoD: Why They're Not the Same Number
item.description: Why SoC and DoD are two views of the same battery, how SoC is actually estimated in the field, and why chemistry sets the DoD limit that protects cycle life.

item.title: Cut & Fill Volume: How the Average End Area Method Actually Works
item.description: How earthwork volume between two cross-sections is estimated by averaging their areas, why section spacing controls accuracy, and where the method breaks down.

item.title: Flame Retardant vs Flame Resistant Cables: Know the Difference
item.description: IEC 60332 vs IEC 60331 explained — why flame retardant cables stop fire from spreading while flame (fire) resistant cables keep circuits alive during a fire.

item.title: Grade & Slope: Why Percent, Ratio and Degrees Aren't the Same Number
item.description: How rise over run converts between percent grade, a ratio like 1:20, and an angle in degrees — and why mixing up the three is a common site-drawing mistake.

item.title: Manning's Equation: How Pipe Slope, Roughness and Diameter Set Flow Capacity
item.description: How Manning's equation turns pipe slope, roughness and diameter into gravity flow capacity, why full-bore isn't peak capacity, and what the roughness coefficient actually represents.

item.title: Row Spacing & Inter-Row Shading: Sizing the Gap Between Solar Rows
item.description: Why ground-mount and rooftop solar rows need a minimum gap, how the winter-solstice sun angle sets that gap, and the ground coverage ratio trade-off behind it.

item.title: String vs Microinverter vs Power Optimizer: Choosing a Solar Inverter Topology
item.description: How string inverters, microinverters and power optimizers actually differ in where MPPT happens, what a shaded panel costs you under each, and how to pick between them.

item.title: Solar System Sizing: From Daily Load to Panel Count
item.description: How to go from a daily energy load in kWh to an array size in kW, why peak sun hours (not daylight hours) is the number that matters, and where the derating factors go.

item.title: Stakeholder Power-Interest Grid: Sorting Attention, Not Just People
item.description: How the power-interest grid sorts stakeholders into four engagement strategies, why the same person can move between quadrants, and why 'keep everyone happy' isn't a strategy.

item.title: 33/11 kV Substation: Single Line Diagram & Equipment Overview
item.description: How a 33/11 kV substation is built, walked through its single line diagram from incoming line to distribution feeders — every major equipment item, its function, and the protection schemes that back it up.

item.title: Essential Protection Settings of Air Circuit Breakers (ACB) Explained
item.description: LTPU, LTD, STPU, STD, instantaneous and ground fault settings on an Air Circuit Breaker (ACB) — what each protection parameter does, typical setting ranges, and why the settings exist as a coordinated set, not individual dials.

item.title: Access Control System (ACS) Explained: Components, Architecture & Site Work
item.description: How an Access Control System actually works — main components, the six-step credential-to-unlock sequence, system architecture, integration with FAS/BMS/CCTV, and what an electrical site engineer does on an ACS install.

item.title: AHU, FAHU, FCU, FMAHU, CSAHU: What Is the Difference?
item.description: What separates an AHU, FAHU, FCU, FMAHU and CSAHU — air source, installation style and typical application for each, in one comparison.

item.title: Air Changes per Hour: What ACH Actually Tells You (and Doesn't)
item.description: What air changes per hour (ACH) measures, the formula behind it, typical ACH targets by space type.

item.title: Alarm Setpoint Bands: Why High and High-High Are Different Alarms
item.description: Why alarms come in High/High-High and Low/Low-Low pairs, not single trip points, and how a reset deadband on each keeps the alarm list from flooding operators.

item.title: ANSI Relay Numbers: Common Protection Relay Functions
item.description: A working reference for the ANSI device numbers you'll actually run into on protection schemes — 50/51, 27/59, 87, 21, 67, 25 and more.

item.title: ATS, MTS, ECB & Switch Disconnectors: Transfer & Isolation Switching Devices Explained
item.description: ATS, MTS, COS, switch disconnectors, load break switches, fused switch disconnectors, ECBs, maintenance bypass switches and key interlocks — what each device does, how it differs, and where it's used.

item.title: Beam Bending Basics: Why Section Modulus Decides Capacity, Not Just Load
item.description: Why a beam's bending capacity comes down to two separate checks — bending stress against section modulus, and deflection against span — not just the applied load.

item.title: Bearing Failures: Root Causes & Prevention
item.description: The five most common ways rolling-element bearings actually fail — spalling, lubrication breakdown, contamination, electrical erosion, and false brinelling.

item.title: Belt Drive Sizing: Why the Speed Ratio Alone Doesn't Tell You the Tension
item.description: Belt drive speed ratio, belt velocity and shaft torque from pulley diameters and power, and why tension depends on wrap angle and friction, not just geometry.

item.title: BMS Point Types Explained: AI, AO, BI, BO, MI, MO, BV, AV, MV
item.description: What each BMS point abbreviation actually means — AI, AO, BI, BO, MI, MO, BV, AV and MV.
